requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation in `requirements.ci.span` maps to code with an {impl} reference and to a test with a {test} reference.

**Code:** `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs` does the fence parsing, with `colon_fence` as its helper. `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` builds the trimmed body text.

| Obligation | Code | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Opening fence has at least 3 colons, immediately followed by `{req} <name>` | `colon_fence` requires at least 3 colons. `definition_blocks` then requires the suffix to start with `{req}` and a whitespace-separated name. | `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` in `src/lib.rs` rejects `::{req}`, `::: {req}` and `:::{req}ready`. |
| Closing fence has at least as many colons as the opening one, with nothing else on its line except whitespace | The close search in `definition_blocks` (and `closes` in `src/fenced.rs`) requires `count >= fence_length` and `suffix.trim().is_empty()`. | The same test shows `:::foo` does not close and `::: ` does. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` shows a shorter `:::` does not close a `::::` fence. |
| Up to 3 spaces of indent are allowed, and 4 or more MUST NOT make a fence | `colon_fence` returns `None` when the indent is greater than 3. | The same test covers a three-space-indented opening and closing pair. It also shows that a four-space opening is not a block and that a four-space closing does not close. |
| Body is all Markdown between the fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams and blank lines | `body_start` is the end of the opening line and `body_end` is the start of the closing line. Candidate closing lines that overlap code blocks are skipped. | `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` uses a body with a code block containing `:::`, headings and a setext heading. `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` uses a body with a code example. |
| Body MUST NOT include text after the closing fence | `body_end` stops at the closing line. | `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` places "Outside the requirement." after the fence and a following requirement, and validation passes. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` asserts the outside text is not in the body. |
| Leading and trailing whitespace excluded when comparing with evidence | `collect_definitions` stores the body as `.trim()` text. `validate_evidence_file` compares the evidence string to it exactly. | `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` uses a body with leading blank lines and trailing spaces. |

An unclosed block is reported by `collect_definitions`, and `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` tests that.

One point could be read two ways. The whitespace clause could be read as trimming only the body, or as trimming both the body and the evidence string. The code trims only the body. `requirements.ci.requirement_text` says the evidence string must match the body "excluding leading and trailing whitespace", which fits the body-only reading, so I did not treat this as a gap.

text: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
The `requirement` string in each evidence file MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.
